description: Terraform: new shared stack terraform-shared/ (ECR repos dfi-frontend and dfi-backend, lifecycle policies, GitHub OIDC role limited to one repo and one branch) and per-cluster add-on IAM in terraform/ (EBS CSI managed add-on via Pod Identity, AWS Load Balancer Controller role, policy file and Pod Identity association). Covers plan.md items 1 to 4. Independent of FEAT-003 and later backend/frontend work; FEAT-002 depends on the outputs and names defined here.
steps: Item 1: create c:\Devops\Repository\Developer-friendly-infra\terraform-shared\provider.tf, variables.tf, backend.hcl.example following terraform\provider.tf and terraform\backend.hcl.example. State key developer-friendly-infra/_shared/terraform.tfstate (decision D1). github_org and github_repo have no default.

Item 2: create terraform-shared\main.tf (aws_ecr_repository for_each IMMUTABLE/scan_on_push/AES256/force_delete=false, aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy with untagged rule priority 1 and any rule priority 2, OIDC provider count switch plus data lookup, trust policy with StringEquals on aud and sub, role, inline ECR policy limited to the two repo ARNs), outputs.tf (ecr_repository_urls, ci_role_arn, github_oidc_provider_arn, github_secret_name=AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, instruction), README.md. Read the aws_iam_openid_connect_provider doc first for thumbprint_list.

Item 3: create terraform\ebs-csi.tf (Pod Identity trust for pods.eks.amazonaws.com, role ${local.name}-ebs-csi, AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy attachment); edit terraform\main.tf addons map with aws-ebs-csi-driver and pod_identity_association (service account name confirmed from the AWS doc); add output ebs_csi_role_arn to terraform\outputs.tf. vpc_id output already exists.

Item 4: fetch the LBC IAM policy at tag v3.6.2 with web_fetch mode full, write terraform\policies\aws-load-balancer-controller-iam-policy.json in chunks and re-read to check it is complete (or write the PLACEHOLDER-NOT-VALID-JSON file with the curl command if the fetch fails); create terraform\lbc.tf (policy, role, attachment, aws_eks_pod_identity_association for kube-system/aws-load-balancer-controller); add output lbc_role_arn.

Append a '## FEAT-001' section to c:\Devops\Repository\devops-microservices-platform\.agents\tasks\phase3-idp\verification.md (create it with a header if missing) listing each check, the exact command, and PASSED or UNVERIFIED, plus any placeholder left in the files.
acceptance_criteria: terraform-shared has provider.tf, variables.tf, main.tf, outputs.tf, README.md, backend.hcl.example with the variables, validations and no defaults for github_org/github_repo exactly as in plan.md items 1 and 2

ECR repos are IMMUTABLE, scan_on_push true, AES256, force_delete false, with the two lifecycle rules; the CI role policy names only ecr:GetAuthorizationToken on * and the seven push/pull actions on the two repo ARNs
The OIDC trust uses StringEquals on sub = repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/<branch> and create_github_oidc_provider defaults to false with a data lookup

terraform\main.tf addons include aws-ebs-csi-driver with pod_identity_association; ebs-csi.tf and lbc.tf exist; outputs ebs_csi_role_arn and lbc_role_arn exist; no existing output or protection was removed
The LBC policy file is the full official JSON for v3.6.2 or an obvious PLACEHOLDER-NOT-VALID-JSON file with the download command, never invented content

Running 'cd terraform && terraform fmt -check -recursive && terraform init -backend=false -input=false && terraform validate' and the same in terraform-shared passes (or is recorded UNVERIFIED with the commands; an expected validate failure caused by a placeholder policy file is recorded as such)
verification: cd c:/Devops/Repository/Developer-friendly-infra/terraform-shared && terraform fmt -check -recursive && terraform init -backend=false -input=false && terraform validate
cd c:/Devops/Repository/Developer-friendly-infra/terraform && terraform fmt -check -recursive && terraform init -backend=false -input=false && terraform validate

python -c "import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))" c:/Devops/Repository/Developer-friendly-infra/terraform/policies/aws-load-balancer-controller-iam-policy.json   (only if the real policy was written)
If the shell is down: re-read every new .tf file for balanced braces and resource references, and mark the commands UNVERIFIED in verification.md
findings: Files created in Developer-friendly-infra: terraform-shared/{provider.tf,variables.tf,main.tf,outputs.tf,README.md,backend.hcl.example}; terraform/{ebs-csi.tf,lbc.tf,policies/aws-load-balancer-controller-iam-policy.json}. Edited terraform/main.tf (addon aws-ebs-csi-driver with pod_identity_association) and terraform/outputs.tf (ebs_csi_role_arn, lbc_role_arn). Nothing removed. Names for later steps: shared state key developer-friendly-infra/_shared/terraform.tfstate; ECR repos dfi-frontend and dfi-backend; CI role default name dfi-github-actions-ecr; shared outputs ecr_repository_urls (map), ci_role_arn, github_oidc_provider_arn, github_secret_name (AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN), github_secret_instruction; github_org and github_repo have no default; github_branch default main; create_github_oidc_provider default false. Per-cluster IAM names: <cluster>-ebs-csi and <cluster>-aws-lbc. LBC Pod Identity association is kube-system/aws-load-balancer-controller, so the Helm chart must set serviceAccount.name aws-load-balancer-controller and need no role annotation. EBS CSI service account ebs-csi-controller-sa. LBC policy file is the real v3.6.2 JSON (16 statements, checked by re-reading), not a placeholder. No CHECK-LATEST-FROM placeholders left. Deviation: EBS CSI managed policy ARN is arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicyV2 as named in the current AWS doc (plan listed the older name); switch if plan reports it missing. UNVERIFIED (shell returned Exit Code -1): terraform fmt/init/validate in terraform-shared and terraform, and json.load of the policy file. Exact commands are in verification.md under ## FEAT-001. RUNBOOK.md (item 17) should include the curl command to re-download the LBC policy when the chart is bumped. VERSIONS.md values-to-confirm table: no new rows from FEAT-001, but note the V2 policy ARN.
